name: Organizations (general)
author: Molfar
description: Guilds, orders, companies, gangs, agencies, cults and clans for stories across many genres.

entries.name: Guild of Patient Locksmiths
entries.desc: A guild of locksmiths who never pick a lock without being asked three times. Their keys are said to open doors in dreams.

entries.name: The Honeyed Ledger
entries.desc: A merchant house that deals only in sweets, spices and promises. Its books are bound in beeswax.

entries.name: Sisters of the Lamp-Oil
entries.desc: A small order of lamp-keepers who walk the roads at night refilling roadside lanterns and trading news.

entries.name: Brindle & Daughters
entries.desc: A family company of cartographers who sell maps of places that do not exist yet.

entries.name: Wardens of the Hollow Oak
entries.desc: A circle of foresters who protect a single ancient oak and the secret room inside it.

entries.name: The Court of Small Favors
entries.desc: A loose guild of neighbors who trade minor magic favors under a strict ledger of debts and thanks.

entries.name: Tideglass Collegium
entries.desc: A school of sailors-turned-scholars who study the moods of the sea and write tide-songs.

entries.name: House Marrowbright
entries.desc: A noble house famed for its glassblowers, who fashion drinking cups that warn of poison.

entries.name: The Wandering Bellwrights
entries.desc: A caravan guild that forges and installs bells for villages, each tuned to the village's voice.

entries.name: Order of the Open Hand
entries.desc: An order of healers who take vows to never refuse treatment, and keep a very long waiting list.

entries.name: Thimbletongue Troupe
entries.desc: A band of traveling players whose plays are rumored to alter the weather.

entries.name: The Sentinel Cobblers
entries.desc: A guild of shoemakers who guard border roads, believing every road should be walked in good boots.

entries.name: Candlemakers of the North Fork
entries.desc: A clan of chandlers who make candles that burn only for the truthful.

entries.name: The Pale Quill
entries.desc: A society of scribes who write letters for the dead to the living, for a modest donation.

entries.name: Hearthwatch Company
entries.desc: Hired guardians of inns and taverns, trained to break up brawls without breaking furniture.

entries.name: The Moss Syndicate
entries.desc: A band of herbalists and smugglers who move rare plants across borders.

entries.name: Stonesinger Fellowship
entries.desc: Masons who coax stone into shape with chants. Their cathedrals hum when touched.

entries.name: Cloudreeve Bureau
entries.desc: A bureaucratic office that classifies, names and taxes cloud formations.

entries.name: The Barnacle Lodge
entries.desc: An old fraternity of ship's carpenters who meet in a beached hull and keep their rites underwater.

entries.name: Saltwife Confederacy
entries.desc: A matriarchal league of salt traders who set the price of preserved goods across three kingdoms.

entries.name: Brother Tansy's Almoners
entries.desc: A mendicant order that carries food to the stranded and keeps a record of every name they feed.

entries.name: The Gilded Thimble
entries.desc: A tailors' guild known for cloaks that make the wearer unnoticed in crowds.

entries.name: Greenwatch Rangers
entries.desc: A volunteer band who protect hedgerows and wild paths from developers and wolves.

entries.name: The Weathervane Society
entries.desc: Scholars who read wind patterns and sell forecasts to farmers and kings.

entries.name: Kindle & Ash
entries.desc: A pair of rival apothecary houses who feud by quietly curing each other's patients.

entries.name: The Silverwing Post
entries.desc: A courier company that delivers messages by trained birds, bats and the odd patient owl.

entries.name: Order of Stilled Waters
entries.desc: Contemplatives who guard sacred pools and decide which questions may be asked of them.

entries.name: The Tinker's Parliament
entries.desc: A fractious assembly of traveling repairers who vote by lifting their hammers.

entries.name: Hallowmere Bakers
entries.desc: A bakers' guild whose loaves are blessed for travelers and said to feed twice as many as they should.

entries.name: The Orchard Compact
entries.desc: An alliance of fruit growers who set harvest dates and punish thieves with polite shame.

entries.name: The Ashen Tithe
entries.desc: A church tax collective that takes a portion of every harvest and a measure of every sorrow.

entries.name: Brotherhood of the Last Candle
entries.desc: A monastic order that keeps vigil over dying villages and records their final hours.

entries.name: The Gravewrights
entries.desc: A guild of coffin makers and tomb-builders who bargain with the dead for their trade secrets.

entries.name: Hollowmen of the Fen
entries.desc: A secretive society of bog-dwelling exiles who cut peat and bury what they find in it.

entries.name: The Veiled Court
entries.desc: A shadow tribunal that judges the living by the testimony of ghosts.

entries.name: Order of the Hanged Saint
entries.desc: An order of flagellants who wear nooses as rosaries and walk from town to town.

entries.name: The Bone Auction House
entries.desc: A trader of relics and remains with a long history of both piety and fraud.

entries.name: The Thornwood Covenant
entries.desc: A circle of hedge-witches who bind their members through shared wounds.

entries.name: Sallow Brotherhood
entries.desc: A cult of the plague-struck who believe sickness is a form of grace.

entries.name: The Quiet Surgeons
entries.desc: A secret guild of surgeons who operate on the doomed and do not talk about the results.

entries.name: Hollow Crown Cabal
entries.desc: Nobles who rule through a puppet king and have long forgotten whose face is under the mask.

entries.name: The Salt-and-Iron Watch
entries.desc: Mercenary guards hired to protect towns from what walks at night. They are paid in coin and prayers.

entries.name: Maiden's Hand Sisterhood
entries.desc: A convent of knife-wielding nuns who dispatch the unfaithful with a prayer.

entries.name: The Marrow Merchants
entries.desc: Dealers in bone-powder and grave-dust, supplying alchemists and the curious.

entries.name: Harrow Company
entries.desc: A band of sellswords who hire out to besieged cities, collecting final payment in whatever the survivors own.

entries.name: The Candled Choir
entries.desc: A choir of blind monks whose chants are said to hold back the dark.

entries.name: The Rooks' Parliament
entries.desc: A council of cloaked scavengers who trade intelligence for carrion.

entries.name: Cairnwatch Wardens
entries.desc: Guards of the borderlands who build memorial cairns for those they fail to save.

entries.name: The Woeful Hunt
entries.desc: A band of hunters pursuing a monster that has already killed their founders.

entries.name: Lazarine Order
entries.desc: Monks who attempt to revive the dead and keep the results behind locked doors.

entries.name: The Ember Lantern
entries.desc: A smugglers' ring that guides fugitives across haunted borders with enchanted lamps.

entries.name: Sunless Almsmen
entries.desc: Beggars who sit before shrines and carry curses for hire.

entries.name: The Hollow Inquest
entries.desc: Inquisitors who question corpses and often disagree with the verdict.

entries.name: The Skein of Pale Hands
entries.desc: A cult of weavers who spin burial cloth from the hair of the departed.

entries.name: The Barrow Kings
entries.desc: Grave-robbers who have organized into a mock-nobility with ranks and titles.

entries.name: Tallow & Tears
entries.desc: A funeral company that supplies professional mourners and fine hearses to the wealthy.

entries.name: Order of the Cold Furnace
entries.desc: Smiths who forge blades from relics and nightmares.

entries.name: The Dust Prelates
entries.desc: Clergy in a ruined cathedral who preach to empty pews and the occasional listener.

entries.name: The Briarwives
entries.desc: Village women who protect their homes with thorn charms and old grudges.

entries.name: Wake of the Drowned
entries.desc: A fisherman's guild whose members have all been briefly dead. They speak in sea-lore.

entries.name: Halcyon Freight Union
entries.desc: A union of long-haul pilots who bargain collectively over rest hours, hazard pay and the right to unscheduled stops.

entries.name: The Orbital Cartographic Survey
entries.desc: A planetary survey agency that maps new worlds and keeps its findings sealed for a generation.

entries.name: Quill & Servo
entries.desc: A publishing house run by android editors who refuse to print anything that was machine-written.

entries.name: Deepwell Salvage Collective
entries.desc: A cooperative of salvagers who dismantle wrecked starships and share the proceeds by lottery.

entries.name: The Lantern Fleet
entries.desc: A convoy of refugee ships that travels between stars under a single elected captain.

entries.name: Parallax Dynamics
entries.desc: A corporation that builds precise instruments, famed for its stubborn customer service.

entries.name: The Dome Council
entries.desc: A council of colony delegates who govern a small domed settlement by consensus, unanimity and long meetings.

entries.name: Meridian Biologics
entries.desc: A genetics firm that designs hardy crops and the occasional unlicensed pet.

entries.name: Thistle Relay Authority
entries.desc: A commission that regulates interstellar mail and has grown eccentric from boredom.

entries.name: The Cold Sleep Society
entries.desc: A club of long-sleepers who agree to wake in sequence and pass notes to the future.

entries.name: Stationmasters' Guild
entries.desc: Managers of space stations who share hard-won advice about leaks, pests and angry guests.

entries.name: The Gradient Institute
entries.desc: A research center studying gravity wells, famed for its cheerful maintenance staff and its strange sabbaticals.

entries.name: Brass Pilgrims
entries.desc: A religious order of engineers who treat starships as sacred and travel from port to port blessing engines.

entries.name: The Void Choir
entries.desc: A touring orchestra that performs in zero gravity, selling recordings of silence between movements.

entries.name: Ironwood Colonial Charter
entries.desc: A settlement company that offers land on cold worlds to anyone who will sign a thick contract.

entries.name: Ember Reach Cooperative
entries.desc: A mining cooperative on a lava moon, governed by shifts and a rotating chair.

entries.name: The Seed Archive Trust
entries.desc: Keepers of genetic vaults who lend out samples to fledgling colonies.

entries.name: Pale Ledger Bank
entries.desc: A bank that accepts reputation as collateral, with an auditing division of unsettling accuracy.

entries.name: The Hollow Ship Syndicate
entries.desc: Smugglers who hide cargo inside decommissioned hulls and file them as scrap.

entries.name: Orrery Academy
entries.desc: A school of navigators trained to plot courses by memory when instruments fail.

entries.name: Sable Dock Brotherhood
entries.desc: A dockworkers' mutual aid society that runs strikes, funerals and an excellent soup kitchen.

entries.name: The Long Count Observers
entries.desc: Watchers who record rare cosmic events and keep a poker game going between them.

entries.name: Tinwhistle Courier Service
entries.desc: A discreet delivery service that carries sensitive packages and no questions.

entries.name: The Quiet Registry
entries.desc: An agency that records every artificial mind and tracks their retirements and unexpected grudges.

entries.name: Cradle Station Midwives
entries.desc: A medical order specializing in birth and early life in low gravity.

entries.name: The Spinward Compact
entries.desc: A trade alliance of independent stations with a shared currency and a shared dislike of tariffs.

entries.name: Reclamation Bureau 12
entries.desc: A government unit that restores abandoned colonies and often finds why they were abandoned.

entries.name: Mirror Fleet Inc.
entries.desc: A corporation selling reflective solar sails and a stubbornly optimistic brochure.

entries.name: Cartridge Monks
entries.desc: A scholar order that preserves old data formats and reads forgotten files for fees.

entries.name: The Weathered Hands
entries.desc: A guild of hull repairers who work outside in suits, famous for their quiet superstition.

entries.name: Dunmore & Pike Removals
entries.desc: A family moving company whose drivers know every back road and every secret in town.

entries.name: The Tuesday Night Quizzers
entries.desc: A pub quiz team with a decades-old rivalry and an unexpected network of favors.

entries.name: Greywater Tenants' Union
entries.desc: A residents' association that fights landlords with petitions, potluck dinners and a very large spreadsheet.

entries.name: Harbor Street Mutual
entries.desc: A small credit union with a long memory and a suspicious loan officer.

entries.name: Night Owl Courier Co-op
entries.desc: A bike courier collective that works after midnight and knows every shortcut.

entries.name: The Allotment Society
entries.desc: A committee of garden plot holders whose disputes rival parliamentary debates.

entries.name: Fourth Bell Volunteer Fire Brigade
entries.desc: A volunteer fire crew that doubles as the town's social club.

entries.name: Plum & Sons Locksmiths
entries.desc: A shop that opens doors for any reason and writes down nobody's name.

entries.name: Redwater Community Radio
entries.desc: A volunteer radio station with a loyal audience and a feud over the playlist.

entries.name: The Quiet Hour Book Club
entries.desc: A secretive book club that reads banned novels and trades them in plain brown covers.

entries.name: Pennant Street Football Supporters
entries.desc: A fan group whose chants have gained local fame and whose scarves have been sewn for three generations.

entries.name: Lowland Insurance Group
entries.desc: A mid-sized insurer, notorious for its fine print and its warm holiday cards.

entries.name: The Basement Press
entries.desc: A small independent publisher run from a cellar by three stubborn editors.

entries.name: Cleanslate Cleaners
entries.desc: A cleaning crew that finds more than dust in the buildings they clear, and keeps a locked drawer of it.

entries.name: Blue Door Counseling
entries.desc: A small clinic whose waiting room is known for its overgrown plant and unexpected friendships.

entries.name: The Corner Shop Alliance
entries.desc: A group of local grocers who share stock, gossip and a strict boycott list.

entries.name: Kestrel Taxi Company
entries.desc: A small taxi firm whose drivers keep their own rules and their own radio language.

entries.name: Marlow Park Running Club
entries.desc: A jogging club that meets at dawn and settles every dispute with a lap.

entries.name: Spindle Lane Seamstress Collective
entries.desc: Alteration experts who repair clothes, dignity and the occasional rumor.

entries.name: Granary Row Temp Agency
entries.desc: A staffing agency that places workers in odd roles and has a surprisingly thick file on everyone.

entries.name: The Evening Edition
entries.desc: A local newspaper with a small staff, a great archive and a long list of stories it should not run.

entries.name: Sunday Market Traders
entries.desc: A weekend market association whose stall licenses are inherited like titles.

entries.name: Old Bridge Rowing Club
entries.desc: A rowing club on a river, proud of its trophies and its feud with the club across the water.

entries.name: Station Road Pawnbrokers
entries.desc: A pawnshop with an honest reputation and a back room of curious deposits.

entries.name: Marrow & Pike Associates
entries.desc: A mid-tier law practice that has defended almost everyone in town at least once.

entries.name: Neighborhood Watch Group 14
entries.desc: A volunteer watch that is better at gossip than at patrol.

entries.name: The Last Orders Choir
entries.desc: A pub choir that sings on closing night and refuses to take requests.

entries.name: Lamplight Legal Aid
entries.desc: A free legal clinic run by retired attorneys and strong tea.

entries.name: Canal Boat Residents' Association
entries.desc: Live-aboard boaters who keep a rota for locks, mooring and mischief.

entries.name: Quill Street Tutors
entries.desc: A tutoring agency that has quietly raised half the town's university students.

entries.name: Kuroshio Ripperdocs Co-op
entries.desc: A cooperative of back-alley surgeons who share clients, tools and a pooled legal fund.

entries.name: Glassbreak Runners
entries.desc: A crew of data thieves who specialize in corporate towers and always leave a signature.

entries.name: Lowvolt Collective
entries.desc: A guild of electricians who keep the slums powered and refuse to answer to any corporation.

entries.name: The Sixth District Rats
entries.desc: A street gang of tunnel kids who own the abandoned subway and trade in scavenged parts.

entries.name: Tern Hollow Mutual
entries.desc: An insurance megacorp that prices lives in real time and sends polite drones to collect.

entries.name: Chromium Saints
entries.desc: A gang of augmented bikers who ride in formation and give out free repairs on Sundays.

entries.name: Redline Couriers
entries.desc: A courier agency whose riders carry stolen files and have a rating system by blood type.

entries.name: The Pale Server Church
entries.desc: A cult that worships a dormant AI and pays dues in processing time.

entries.name: Quillfern Biolabs
entries.desc: A pharmaceutical firm that sells designer cravings with a lifetime subscription.

entries.name: Gutterlight Press
entries.desc: An underground press that prints truth on stolen billboards.

entries.name: Fixer's Row Syndicate
entries.desc: A union of fixers who broker jobs and keep a communal blacklist.

entries.name: Tin Heart Gang
entries.desc: A gang of androids who escaped a factory and now guard their old assembly line from its owners.

entries.name: Mirrorwall Security
entries.desc: A corporate security contractor with a slogan about peace of mind and a policy of shoot first.

entries.name: Meridian Quay Smuggling Family
entries.desc: A smuggling family that moves cargo by cargo drone.

entries.name: The Static Choir
entries.desc: A hacker collective that hijacks billboards to broadcast hymns.

entries.name: Neon Tide Aid
entries.desc: A street clinic that treats drug addicts and glitching cyborgs with equal care and no paperwork.

entries.name: Slate Harbour Arms
entries.desc: A weapons maker that sells to every side, and has a fashion line.

entries.name: The Eyeless
entries.desc: A gang that tore out their own cameras and implants to hide from surveillance.

entries.name: Vermilion Logistics
entries.desc: A shipping firm with an armed drone escort and a very odd definition of damage.

entries.name: The Wirebound
entries.desc: A subculture of hackers who permanently jack in, speaking in nested slang.

entries.name: Backstreet Pharmacy Network
entries.desc: A string of unlicensed pharmacies that move stock between homes by courier.

entries.name: The Dust Council
entries.desc: A council of scavengers who run the garbage district with a rule of rotating chairs.

entries.name: Sable Wire Detective Agency
entries.desc: Private investigators who specialize in finding stolen memories and missing identities.

entries.name: Chrome Parish
entries.desc: A congregation that venerates machines and blesses cyberware at its altar.

entries.name: Kestrel Bioworks
entries.desc: A biotech company that sells custom organs and a cheerful warranty.

entries.name: The Overpass Union
entries.desc: Workers who live under elevated highways and strike against corporate rents.

entries.name: Glow Alley Kitchen Collective
entries.desc: A group of street cooks who share recipes, licenses and a legendary hot sauce.

entries.name: Mirage Media
entries.desc: A propaganda studio that produces custom realities for whoever pays.

entries.name: The Last Terminal
entries.desc: A hacker bar that doubles as an arbitration court for disputes over code.

entries.name: Neonbridge Taxi Alliance
entries.desc: Cab drivers who run illegal shortcuts and unlicensed tours.

entries.name: Caravan Wardens
entries.desc: A guild of armed guards for desert caravans, paid in water and trust.

entries.name: The Rust Harvest Co-op
entries.desc: Scavengers who farm old machines for parts and sell what they cannot use.

entries.name: Cistern Keepers
entries.desc: A faction that controls the last clean water tanks and rations by lottery.

entries.name: The Lantern Road Fellowship
entries.desc: A pilgrim band that lights roadside lamps and gives shelter to travelers.

entries.name: Gearhead Gleaners
entries.desc: Mechanics who roam in a convoy of patched trucks, repairing whatever breaks.

entries.name: The Greenhouse Circle
entries.desc: A cooperative that grows food in sealed greenhouses and trades seeds for protection.

entries.name: Hollow Gate Militia
entries.desc: A volunteer defense force guarding a fortified settlement and its mildly unhelpful mayor.

entries.name: Ember Court
entries.desc: A tribunal of elders who settle disputes with coin tosses and long memory.

entries.name: The Scrapwright Kin
entries.desc: A clan of tinkers who build machines from garbage and their own stubborn pride.

entries.name: The Last Library Order
entries.desc: Librarians who protect surviving books and trade reading time for food.

entries.name: Dustwalkers
entries.desc: Nomadic scouts who guide travelers across the wastes and charge by the mile.

entries.name: The Brine Merchants
entries.desc: Salt traders who run a caravan network and keep a steady neutrality.

entries.name: Seedkeepers of the Cold Vault
entries.desc: Guardians of a deep-frozen seed bank, protected by a rotating watch and an unruly dog.

entries.name: Pump Station Seven
entries.desc: A fortified well-house with an elected council and a strict one-cup rule.

entries.name: Moth Eaters
entries.desc: A raider gang that dresses in cloaks made from old curtains and travels at night.

entries.name: The Chime Tribe
entries.desc: A nomadic group that signals with wind chimes and cans.

entries.name: The Concrete Sisters
entries.desc: A women's militia who hold a collapsed overpass settlement.

entries.name: Axle & Ash Haulers
entries.desc: Truckers who run supply routes across ruined highways, armored in scrap.

entries.name: Oilcan Lodge
entries.desc: A fraternity of mechanics with a creed of repair-before-reprisal.

entries.name: The Clean Water Compact
entries.desc: A treaty alliance among settlements to share filtered water and deter poisoners.

entries.name: Raftmen of the Flooded City
entries.desc: Boat-folk who ferry goods through the drowned streets of a ruined metropolis.

entries.name: Bunker Eleven Council
entries.desc: The ruling committee of an underground shelter with strict ration records.

entries.name: The Mender Guild
entries.desc: Tailors and medics who patch wounds and clothes alike, bound by a creed against vengeance.

entries.name: Reapers of the Last Field
entries.desc: Harvesters who guard the last wheat field with scythes and a stern code.

entries.name: Gaslight Traders
entries.desc: A merchant convoy that sells batteries, bulbs and rumors.

entries.name: The Ash Wardens
entries.desc: A band that polices a burned forest and enforces the only law there is.

entries.name: Tin Can Telegraph
entries.desc: A network of wire-and-can messengers who relay news across the ruins.

entries.name: Windmill Kin
entries.desc: A family-run consortium who control the last turbines and distribute power by schedule.

entries.name: The Quiet Scavengers
entries.desc: Salvagers who work in silence, communicating by hand signs, rarely seen.

entries.name: The Greyhound Riders
entries.desc: A pack of motorcycle couriers who carry news and medicine across the wasteland.

entries.name: Honourable Company of Rope Makers
entries.desc: A craft guild regulating hemp and cord, with feasts, apprentices and a very long charter.

entries.name: House of Quill & Seal
entries.desc: A family of notaries who register contracts for merchants and keep every secret in sealed boxes.

entries.name: The Mercers' Hall
entries.desc: A guild of cloth dealers who control the market, set fair prices and settle their quarrels in court.

entries.name: Brothers of the Open Road
entries.desc: A religious order whose monks guide pilgrims and maintain hostels along the pilgrim roads.

entries.name: The Tollkeepers' League
entries.desc: Bridge and gate officials who collect dues and keep a roll of every traveler.

entries.name: Salt Road Caravan Company
entries.desc: A trading company that runs mule trains across mountain passes with fierce discipline.

entries.name: The Chandlers' Fraternity
entries.desc: Candle makers who guard their recipes and meet at the sign of the white wick.

entries.name: The Harbor Pilots' Guild
entries.desc: River and harbor pilots who steer ships safely through sandbanks, for a fee and a bit of pride.

entries.name: Fenland Drainers' Syndicate
entries.desc: A company of engineers who reclaim wetland and are loved or hated according to the harvest.

entries.name: The Wardens of the Beacon
entries.desc: A band of watchers who maintain hilltop signal fires and are paid in grain.

entries.name: Sisters of the Almshouse
entries.desc: A women's charity order that runs a house for the elderly poor.

entries.name: The Silkroad Brokers
entries.desc: A merchant bunch who arrange trade between eastern and western markets, taking a share of every deal.

entries.name: The Armorers' Court
entries.desc: A body of smiths who test, stamp and certify armor, and fine anyone who fakes the mark.

entries.name: The Pewter Guild
entries.desc: Casters of pewter ware who maintain strict standards and public marks.

entries.name: The Brewers' Brotherhood
entries.desc: A guild of ale makers with ancient rights to specific wells and a drinking song.

entries.name: Company of Drovers
entries.desc: Cattle herders who guide herds along old droving roads to distant markets.

entries.name: The Lamplighters' Company
entries.desc: Street lamplighters who work in a tight rota and swap news at dusk.

entries.name: The Bargemen's Fellowship
entries.desc: Canal boatmen who share locks, news and a pooled fund for widows.

entries.name: The Royal Lockmakers
entries.desc: A workshop that designs locks for palaces and prisons, famed for its secretive apprenticeships.

entries.name: Scriveners' Guild
entries.desc: Public writers and copyists, whose regulated fees are posted on the guildhall door.

entries.name: Order of the Silent Bell
entries.desc: A monastic order that sounds a bell at dusk and follows a vow of quiet.

entries.name: The Tanners' Society
entries.desc: Leather workers whose guild sits downwind, rich and unloved.

entries.name: Wool Staplers' Company
entries.desc: Merchants who weigh and grade wool for export, and sit on their own court.

entries.name: The Watch of the Narrow Gate
entries.desc: Town guards who patrol the walls and keep a ledger of every visitor.

entries.name: The Corn Exchange Society
entries.desc: Grain dealers who set the market price and gossip about the harvest.

entries.name: The Bellfounders' Brotherhood
entries.desc: Bronze casters who cast church bells and keep their alloys secret.

entries.name: Society of Apothecaries and Spice Dealers
entries.desc: A trading body of herbalists and spice merchants regulating drugs and flavors.

entries.name: The Ferrymen's Guild
entries.desc: River ferrymen who hold exclusive crossing rights and bar newcomers by custom.

entries.name: Quarantine Board
entries.desc: An official body that inspects ships and decides which may land and which must wait.

entries.name: The Hiring Fair Marshals
entries.desc: Officials who oversee servant and laborer hiring fairs and settle contract disputes.

entries.name: The Society of the Unlit Window
entries.desc: A club of collectors who gather stories about houses with a single dark window, and visit them.

entries.name: Ward Eleven Staff
entries.desc: Night nurses at a ward that no longer appears on the hospital map.

entries.name: The Quiet Parishioners
entries.desc: A congregation that sits in total silence and watches anyone who enters.

entries.name: Blackwater Ferry Company
entries.desc: A boat firm that runs one route at night and never seems to carry anyone back.

entries.name: The Lamplighter's Brotherhood
entries.desc: Lamplighters who keep the lights burning to ward away what waits behind the dark.

entries.name: Pale Hours Funeral Collective
entries.desc: Undertakers who work at night and speak to the departed in low voices.

entries.name: The Fourth Floor Tenants
entries.desc: Residents of a building whose fourth floor does not exist, but still sends rent notices.

entries.name: The Candlewick Seance Club
entries.desc: A hobby circle that holds weekly seances, and has begun to receive replies.

entries.name: The Last Bus Riders
entries.desc: A group of strangers who always ride the same late bus and avoid looking at the driver.

entries.name: Cellar Door Society
entries.desc: A club that explores unlisted basements, keeping a dwindling roster.

entries.name: The Wake Keepers
entries.desc: Mourners paid to sit up with the dead, who have begun to answer when addressed.

entries.name: Hollow Doll Maker's Guild
entries.desc: Toy makers whose creations are said to move when no one is looking.

entries.name: The Closed Casket Club
entries.desc: A fraternity of people who all attended the same funeral and agree never to discuss it.

entries.name: Order of the Held Breath
entries.desc: A cult that practices long silence and long dives, believing the deep listens.

entries.name: The Night Shift Cleaners
entries.desc: Cleaners at an old school who stay after hours and do not discuss what they mop.

entries.name: Mourner's Mutual
entries.desc: A burial society that guarantees a funeral to every member, whatever the cost.

entries.name: Candle & Key Sisterhood
entries.desc: Nuns who guard a locked room in their convent and rotate their watch every night.

entries.name: The Hollow Orchestra
entries.desc: Musicians who play in an abandoned hall and cannot be heard by the living.

entries.name: The Moth Choir
entries.desc: A choral group that rehearses in empty churches and attracts moths in huge numbers.

entries.name: The Gravel Pit Search Party
entries.desc: Volunteers who comb a flooded quarry every year, never finding the same body twice.

entries.name: The Pale Gardeners
entries.desc: Caretakers of a cemetery garden whose roses bloom at the wrong season.

entries.name: Lanterns of the Lost
entries.desc: A charity that leaves lit lanterns on roads where travelers have vanished.

entries.name: The Mirror Watchers
entries.desc: A fellowship who guard antique mirrors and know which ones to cover.

entries.name: Parish of Unspoken Names
entries.desc: A congregation forbidden to say the name of their patron saint.

entries.name: The Hollow Carnival Players
entries.desc: A traveling troupe whose act is the same every night, and every audience has forgotten before dawn.

entries.name: The Long Table Society
entries.desc: Dinner guests invited each year to a feast whose host never appears.

entries.name: The Attic Archivists
entries.desc: Archivists in a mansion attic cataloging objects that have started to appear by themselves.

entries.name: Sleepwalkers' Aid Society
entries.desc: A volunteer group that follows sleepwalkers to prevent harm, and has begun to notice where they go.

entries.name: The Understairs Congregation
